agency: Metropolitan Police Department of the District of Columbia
outcome_detail: Settled in October 2022; the defendants agreed to compensate the plaintiff for his injuries, but the settlement amount was not publicly disclosed in available reporting. Before settlement, the court in March 2022 granted partial summary judgment for the plaintiff, holding unconstitutional the D.C. law permitting searches of people based solely on warrants to search premises (Mwimanzi v. Wilson, 590 F. Supp. 3d 231 (D.D.C. 2022)).
criminal_detail: No criminal charges against Officer Joshua Wilson were reported in the coverage or case materials reviewed.
description: The ACLU of D.C. filed suit on January 13, 2020 in the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia (Mwimanzi v. Wilson, No. 1:20-cv-00079) on behalf of a 33-year-old District resident against Metropolitan Police Department Officer Joshua Wilson. The suit alleged that during a January 15, 2019 execution of a drug search warrant at a Petworth apartment, Wilson conducted a warrantless, sexually invasive bodily search, pressing into the man's buttocks and anus and repeatedly rubbing and jamming his testicles, causing severe pain and yielding no evidence. The complaint claimed violations of the Fourth Amendment and battery under D.C. law. In March 2022 the court granted partial summary judgment for the plaintiff, holding unconstitutional the D.C. law that permitted searches of people based on warrants to search places. In October 2022 the defendants agreed to a settlement compensating the plaintiff; the amount was not publicly disclosed.
notes: Filed before 2021; included because resolution occurred in window (settled October 2022). ACLU-DC reported this was its fourth suit in recent years over sexually invasive searches by D.C. officers.
